thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for tenant montclair (vpc-montclair-prod). High 5xx ratio observed starting 2026-03-17T10:42:11Z — current error rate 22%. Canary rollout at 10:40 UTC suspected. Link: https://redwood.ops/incident/3661239876
erica: oncall here, looking. assigning initial triage.
montclair-sre: hi — we're seeing a spike in 500s and GPU OOMs right after the canary push. Can confirm canary shard 3 started failing around 10:41.
samir: pulling logs now. quick snippet: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating KVCache (size=2.1G)` from model-worker-3.
jia: any change in tokenization or batch config in this canary?
montclair-sre: yes, tokenizer v2.1 was included, and batch_size default bumped to 8 in the canary artifact. We've suspected cache growth but didn't hit this scale in qa.
erica: what's the canary traffic % for montclair? need to decide divert vs pin.
deploy-bot: Canary traffic: tenant montclair -> 12% of requests to canary (approx 120 req/min), burst peaks ~420 req/min.
montclair-sre: customer is on a dedicated VPC pool (montclair-prod). We want immediate tenant diversion + pin to previous stable artifact.
erica: agreed. plan: 1) divert tenant traffic off canary to stable pool 2) pin pool artifact to last known good 3) disable / hold canary for this tenant 4) monitor for error reduction. handoff to samir to execute.
samir: executing now. running commands: ```
rctl tenant divert --tenant montclair --from-pool montclair-canary --to-pool montclair-stable --reason "canary OOM"
rctl artifact pin --pool montclair-prod --artifact montclair/model:2026-02-14-rc5 --force
```
samir: commands returned OK. diversion accepted (propagating), artifact pinned (pinned artifact: montclair/model:2026-02-14-rc5). estimated propagation ~30s.
montclair-sre: seeing traffic transition. new reqs landing on stable instances. 1min window latency median 210ms, errors dropping.
jia: leaving canary disabled for montclair tenant; do not unpublish canary yet — we need to repro.
erica: good. samir, can you keep monitoring for 30m and escalate if errors >2%? I'll open an incident ticket.
samir: monitoring — currently errors down to 0.9% and trending down. I'll stay on for at least 60min.
oncall-ops: acknowledgement. escalation rule set: if tenant error_rate > 2% for 5 min then page SRE lead.
montclair-sre: root cause hypothesis: tokenizer v2.1 increased token split rate leading to larger KV cache usage during generation. Under peak concurrent requests this caused cache blowup and OOM on one canary shard. Repro steps being drafted. Temporary mitigation we applied: reduced KV cache TTL on canary from 1h to 10m and lowered default batch_size to 4 for canary builds.
erica: please add exact repro command and heap dump to the incident ticket. Also loop in ML-infra and customer success for timeline.
montclair-sre: will post artifacts to #montclair-runbook and attach heap dumps + config diff. Also scheduling a deeper canary repro run with reduced batch and cacheguard.
deploy-bot: Canary shard 3 status: READY, errors 0. Overall tenant error rate: 0.4%.
erica: excellent. I'm handing primary monitoring to samir (staying). I'm oncall for another 37 minutes; if anything flares, page me.
samir: noted. I'll keep a close eye and run pre-req checks before any re-roll.
incident-bot: Incident mitigation applied and verified. Creating INC-2026-0317 (montclair canary OOM/pinned rollback). Suspected root cause: tokenizer-change + larger batch leading to KV cache growth and GPU OOM. Action items: (1) RCA with ML + SRE, (2) controlled repro, (3) canary config hardening (batch/cache defaults), (4) gradual safe-rollout checklist.
montclair-sre: customer is notified via email. Montclair SRE requested ETA: we'll aim for a repro + fix PR within 24h, then a staged canary with stricter traffic gating.
erica: thanks. closing active pager for now; samir remains monitor. Please keep this thread updated with the RCA link and timeline. :thumbsup:
